## 4. A direct irreducibility proof

The compact action is
$$
(\pi_n(a,b)f)(q)=\tau_n(b)f(a^{-1}qb).
\tag{C10}
$$
Average over the first factor, with Haar probability measure:
$$
(P_Lf)(q)=\int_{\operatorname{Sp}(1)}f(a^{-1}q)\,da=f(0).
\tag{C11}
$$
For $q\ne0$, this is the spherical mean of the harmonic function $f$ over the sphere of radius $|q|$; for $q=0$ it is immediate. Thus $P_L$ is the orthogonal projection onto the constant $V_n$. The second compact factor acts irreducibly on those constants by $\tau_n$.

Let $M$ be a nonzero closed $G$-invariant subspace. Choose $f\in M$ and a point $p$ with $f(p)\ne0$. Transitivity and the invertible fibre multiplier give a translate $\pi_n(g)f$ nonzero at $0$. Averaging that vector by $P_L$ gives a nonzero constant in $M$. Its second-compact-factor orbit spans the entire constant $V_n$, so $M$ contains every constant.

If $M$ were proper, unitarity would make $M^\perp$ another nonzero closed invariant subspace. The same argument would put all constants in $M^\perp$, a contradiction. Therefore the representation is irreducible. Equivalently, the translates of its constant $V_n$ span a dense subspace.

This proof establishes irreducibility of the whole completed kernel, rather than merely identifying one irreducible subrepresentation inside it.

## 5. An explicit embedding in the regular representation

Fix Haar measure by
$$
\int_G\Phi(g)\,dg=\int_B\int_K\Phi(\sigma(q)k)\,dk\,s(q)^{-4}dv(q),
\qquad \int_Kdk=1
$$
in this disintegration convention. The base measure is invariant. Let $v\in V_n$ be nonzero and $c_v$ its constant function. Use a complex inner product linear in the first argument. Harmonic mean values and the probability measure give
$$
\langle f,c_v\rangle_{\mathcal B_n}=\langle f(0),v\rangle_{V_n}.
$$
The matrix-coefficient map
$$
(\mathcal W_vf)(g)
=\langle\pi_n(g^{-1})f,c_v\rangle
=\langle F_f(g),v\rangle
\tag{C12}
$$
intertwines $\pi_n$ with left translation on functions on $G$.

Schur orthogonality for the finite-dimensional irreducible $\tau_n$ gives
$$
\int_K|\langle\tau_n(k_R)^{-1}u,v\rangle|^2dk
=\frac{\|u\|^2\|v\|^2}{n+1}.
$$
Since $F_f(\sigma(q))=s^{(n+2)/2}f(q)$, we obtain the exact norm identity
$$
\boxed{\|\mathcal W_vf\|_{L^2(G)}^2
=\frac{\|v\|^2}{(n+1)C_n}\,\|f\|_{\mathcal B_n}^2.}
\tag{C13}
$$
Thus a fixed scalar multiple of $\mathcal W_v$ is an isometric embedding with closed invariant image in $L^2(G)$. Together with irreducibility, this proves that $\mathcal B_n$ and $\mathcal H_n$ are discrete series. It removes the need to appeal to an uninspected classification theorem for square-integrability.

For normalized $v$, the inverse constant in (C13) is $n(n^2-1)/\pi^2$ for the specified Haar measure. Its vanishing at the endpoint is consistent with the divergence discussed below; it is not used as a substitute for that argument.
